data.method: run-level bootstrap of the median (4,000 resamples of runs within arm); WLS in log-log weighted by bootstrap SE

pure_power_law.verdict: a single power law T ~ L^1.69 fits the four geometries adequately (p = 0.66)

diffusive_L2_over_full_range.verdict: REJECTED - the neutral arm is not diffusive over 96-768

neutral.crossover_form: T = A L^z0 [1+(L/L_c)^p]^((2-z0)/p), p = 2 (smooth), asymptote z = 2 (diffusive) imposed

crossover_vs_powerlaw_LR.verdict: a crossover to L^2 is NOT required by the data (p = 0.37); adding L_c does not improve the fit significantly

profile_likelihood_free_z0.note: profile is flat (dchi2 < 1) from L_c ~ 100 to infinity; only L_c below ~70-90 is excluded when z0 is free

neutral.L_c: NOT IDENTIFIED. Best-fit L_c depends entirely on the assumed sub-diffusive small-L exponent z0 (L_c ~ 130 for z0 = 1, ~200 for z0 = 4/3, ~310 for z0 = 1.5, ~480 for z0 = 1.6) and is unbounded above; a pure power law fits equally well.
neutral.excluded_range: Any crossover to diffusive L^2 scaling with L_c below the sampled range is excluded (L_c < ~90-210 depending on z0, i.e. L_c below the smallest measured length): the neutral arm is nowhere on the L^2 branch, so the crossover, if it exists, lies at or above the top of the measured range (L_c >~ 200-800) or beyond it.

T_over_L2_diagnostic.verdict: T/L^2 falls monotonically 21.6 -> 12.3 with no plateau: the diffusive asymptote is not reached by L = 768

neutral.statement: No data collapse: with four geometries spanning a factor 8 in L_long, the neutral fixation time is fit by a single apparent power law T ~ L^1.69, and neither the T/L^2 nor the T/L^1.73 rescaling produces a plateau. A Family-Vicsek-style crossover to the diffusive L^2 law fits no better than the pure power law (likelihood-ratio p = 0.37), and its crossover scale L_c is unidentifiable - the profile likelihood is flat from L_c ~ 100 out to infinity, and the fitted L_c tracks whatever small-L exponent is assumed. What the data DO establish: (i) the neutral arm is not diffusive within the measured range (T ~ L^2 rejected, chi2 = 26.4 on 3 dof, p < 1e-5), and (ii) T/L^2 is still falling at L = 768, so any crossover to L^2 lies at or beyond the top of the sampled range - crossover scales L_c below roughly the smallest measured length (~90-210, depending on the assumed small-L exponent) are excluded, but no upper bound can be placed. Identifying L_c would require the neutral arm to reach the L^2 plateau, i.e. lengths at least a factor of a few beyond 768.

constant_velocity_ballistic_T_prop_L.verdict: DECISIVELY REJECTED (dchi2 = 32 vs free fit): fixation is not a constant-speed sweep, so 'T = L / v_eff' with a geometry-independent v_eff is falsified

random_slope_ballistic_sweep_T_prop_sqrt.inputs: kappa ~ L^-0.69, sigma_dR ~ L^-0.76 (fitted to the four L_short=32 geometries)
random_slope_ballistic_sweep_T_prop_sqrt.verdict: CONSISTENT: the loaded arm collapses in the scaling variable L/(kappa sigma_dR), not L/v

homogeneity_test.verdict: the six C values are statistically consistent with a single constant (p = 0.14)

collapse.circularity: kappa and sigma_dR are measured from the SAME loaded fixation runs whose medians they collapse, and C is fitted; this is a one-constant organising relation (internal consistency of the random-slope form), not an independent prediction
collapse.v_eff: the effective drift velocity is not a constant: v(t) = kappa*sigma_dR*t grows linearly (random-slope gap g = dR*t drives the front at speed kappa*g), giving the parabolic sweep h ~ kappa*dR*t^2/2 and hence T ~ sqrt(L/(kappa*sigma_dR)); v_eff at fixation ranges 0.002-0.004 sites/frame across geometries and is set by the drift response kappa and the rate scatter sigma_dR, as the panel anticipated

answer_to_charge: Neutral arm: NO collapse and NO identified L_c - reported honestly as a null result with an exclusion (L_c below ~the smallest measured length is excluded; L_c is unbounded above). Loaded arm: YES, a one-constant scaling collapse in the ballistic-sweep variable sqrt(L/(kappa sigma_dR)) (C = 1.64 +/- 0.11, CV 6.8%, homogeneous across six geometries, p = 0.14), with the constant-velocity ballistic prediction T ~ L decisively rejected; the collapse is internally consistent but not an independent test because its inputs come from the same runs.
